metadata.dataset_description: The dataset combines 1,050 entries from two simulated ServiceNow `sn_gf_goal` tables, capturing various attributes related to organizational goals. These attributes include goal state, owner, department, start and end dates, descriptions, and key performance metrics such as priority, percent complete, and target percentage. The dataset offers a comprehensive view of goal management across departments, with a focus on cross-departmental collaboration, seasonal performance trends, and priority-level efficiency. The data also tracks updates to each goal, documenting the timeline of changes and the individuals responsible for these updates, providing a rich context for analyzing organizational efficiency and strategic goal alignment.
metadata.goal: Analyze the impact of cross-departmental collaboration and seasonal timing on the success rates of organizational goals. Additionally, assess how task priority correlates with completion rates across different categories to optimize resource allocation and strategic planning.

predicted_insights: High-priority goals show the best completion and on-time rates, particularly in Marketing, HR, and Sales, while Critical and Low priorities consistently underperform in timeliness. Marketing leads in High-priority execution, while Sales and Marketing struggle with Critical priorities. Small sample sizes in some category-priority slices contribute to variability, requiring cautious interpretation. Focus on improving on-time rates for Critical and Low priorities and leveraging strengths in High-priority execution.

Success rates for single-department goals peak in Q4 2023 (32.77%) and November 2023 (36.78%), then decline through Q1–Q3 2024, bottoming in Q3 (14.34%). Rates recover in Q4 2024 (29.89%), with October showing improvement. Late 2023 starts outperform most 2024 cohorts, suggesting a need to analyze factors behind the mid-2024 dip and Q4 2024 rebound.
No records exist for `sn_gf_goal` with a start date in Q4 (Oct–Dec), suggesting potential gaps in data or misaligned date ranges that may require verification.
No goal records are currently associated with the IT department in the dataset, potentially due to missing data, alternative naming conventions, or filter issues.
No data is available for goals with a collaborating department specified, indicating the field is either rarely used or currently unpopulated.
There are no goals marked as High priority in the dataset.

Higher completion percentages are positively correlated with meeting goals on time, with the strongest association observed in High-priority tasks (r=0.64). Medium-priority tasks have the largest sample size but a weaker correlation (r=0.53), indicating High-priority work more directly impacts timely goal achievement.

Goal volume peaked in 2024-Q2 but declined sharply by 2024-Q4, where success rates improved to 18% despite fewer goals. Success rates were lowest in 2024-Q3, indicating a rebound in completion efficiency late in the year compared to earlier quarters.

Single-department goals show an average completion of 64.5% and a median of 66%, with only 22% completed on time and 9% achieving ≥90% completion. This highlights a gap between general progress and high-performance outcomes, suggesting a need to review goal timelines and parsing logic for cross-department goals.

Goals generally show strong progress (mean completion 64.10%) but struggle with timeliness (mean on-time delivery 19.66%). High-priority goals dominate completion rates, with High–Customer Satisfaction leading (75.33% completion, 0.40 on-time). Innovation goals perform well in completion but consistently miss deadlines, particularly Medium–Innovation (64.44% completion, 0.14 on-time). Low-priority and critical goals face severe deadline issues, with Low–Process Improvement (0.03 on-time) and Critical–Revenue Growth (0.04 on-time) being the worst performers. Cost Reduction and Innovation categories drive much of the variance, highlighting a completion–timeliness gap that warrants further investigation.

The quartile analysis shows minimal variation, with mean updates consistently at 1 across all quartiles, indicating ineffective stratification by updates. Quartile 3 shows slightly higher completion (66.77%), on-time rate (28%), and success rate (12%), while quartile 4 has the lowest outcomes. Further analysis may require alternative stratification or goals with more updates for meaningful insights.

No goal records exist for the IT department in the dataset, potentially due to naming discrepancies, filters, or missing data.

Percent_complete is positively correlated with goals being met, strongest for High priority (0.56–0.72) and stable across quarters. Medium and Critical priorities show moderate correlations (0.42–0.67 and 0.37–0.62, respectively), while Low priority is weaker and more variable, dipping sharply in 2024-Q3 (0.15). High priority consistently performs best, with no negative correlations observed.

High-priority goals outperform others in on-time rates and completion within common duration buckets (31–90 and 91–180 days), while Critical and Low priorities lag despite similar timelines. Shorter timelines (≤30 days) show higher performance but are based on minimal samples, limiting generalization. No goals exceed 180 days in duration.

From 2023-Q4 to 2024-Q3, success and on-time rates steadily declined, reaching their lowest in 2024-Q3 (success 6%, on-time 14%). In 2024-Q4, both metrics rebounded (success 18%, on-time 30%), though the smaller cohort size suggests potential mix or volume effects. Volume peaked in 2024-Q2 and tapered afterward.

High-priority categories outperform others in both on-time rates (0.36–0.40) and average completion (68–75%), with High–Customer Satisfaction leading. Critical and Low-priority categories underperform significantly, especially Critical–Revenue Growth (on-time 0.04) and Low–Process Improvement (on-time 0.03). Medium-priority categories show moderate performance, with middling timeliness (0.14–0.18) and completion (60–68%). Key areas for improvement include timeliness in Critical–Revenue Growth and Low–Process Improvement, and addressing the lower on-time rate for High–Innovation despite decent completion.
